perplexity.description:
The Big Lebowski (Original Motion Picture Soundtrack), released in 1998, is a genre-spanning compilation that mirrors the eclectic and offbeat tone of the Coen Brothers' cult film. Produced by T Bone Burnett, the album blends electronic, jazz, and rock elements with forays into folk, pop, and country, creating a soundtrack that is as unpredictable as the movie itself. Highlights include the sultry jazz of Henry Mancini’s “Lujon,” the classic rock of The Gipsy Kings’ cover of “Hotel California,” and Carter Burwell’s original electronic-tinged score pieces, which provide a modern, atmospheric backbone to the collection.

While not a traditional artist album, The Big Lebowski soundtrack stands as a signature work in the discographies of its featured artists and producers, particularly T Bone Burnett, whose curatorial touch helped define the film’s unique sonic identity. The soundtrack’s mix of well-known tracks and lesser-known gems—such as Townes Van Zandt’s haunting “Dead Flowers” and the quirky “Technopop” by Burwell—showcases a bold approach to film scoring that eschews convention. Upon its original release, the album received positive critical reception for its inventive selection and seamless integration with the film, and it has since been regarded as one of the standout soundtracks of the late 1990s, celebrated for its eclectic style and enduring influence.
